key_insight: A particle-based shear-flow simulation shows that dense suspensions of granular spherocylinders exhibit a start-up viscosity spike, then reach steady viscosities that rise with particle loading and aspect ratio.
engineering_relevance: The model helps predict how rod-shaped granular suspensions will flow and align, which is useful for designing and processing fibrous or rod-filled materials in manufacturing.
method: Tracks spherocylindrical rods in simple shear flow
Includes short-range frictional contact and hydrodynamic forces
Adds lubrication-force calculations and dynamic timestep control
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic trends in predicted viscosity and microstructure up to aspect ratio 20, with agreement against the limited experimental rheology data available.
watch_item: Validation appears limited by sparse experimental data, so predictions may need further benchmarking for broader particle shapes and flow conditions.
paper_title: Rheology of dense suspensions of granular spherocylinders by particle-based simulation
